name: RYR1
summary: RYR1, malignant hyperthermia (MH) - a dominant disorder of the calcium-release channel of skeletal muscle (c.7360C>G, p.R2454G), so one copy is enough and there is no silent carrier. The horse may seem normal until a trigger, chiefly certain anaesthetics, sets off a life-threatening crisis of overheating and muscle breakdown. Found in the Quarter Horse and related breeds - Paint Horse, Appaloosa and Quarter Horse crosses - at about one allele in a thousand. No living horse with two copies has been confirmed. It can make PSSM1 (GYS1) worse in a horse that has both.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: Malignant hyperthermia
phenotypes.description: One copy of the RYR1 variant. The horse can look and work normally until a trigger - a halogenated anaesthetic, succinylcholine, or sometimes stress, illness or excitement - sets off a crisis: very high temperature, rigid muscles, muscle breakdown, an irregular heartbeat, and in severe episodes death.

phenotypes.name: Two copies (not documented)
phenotypes.description: No living horse with two copies has been confirmed in large-scale testing. The pair may be lethal before or soon after birth, but that is unproven, and what such a horse would be like is unknown.
